headline: Generative models couple single-cell and spatial readouts with external priors
label: Single Cell Computational Methods
summary: Perturbation prediction, histology-to-expression mapping, and mosaic integration now use learned priors to constrain single-cell inference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is model-based inference in which external structure constrains solutions rather than fitting one modality alone. Histology-to-expression work illustrates this: MoSPR pairs morpho-spatial macrostates with a low-rank molecular basis, and GATE-ST fuses LLM-generated gene text summaries with image embeddings via cross-attention. Perturbation models impose structure on transport: DRIFT separates invariant from responsive latent blocks for conditional flow matching, PerturbBridge learns a perturbation-conditioned Schrödinger Bridge, and scEGFlow applies energy guidance to unseen conditions. Crecerelle jointly embeds expression and splicing isoforms, while DR-GEM, the published item, applies self-supervised embeddings to rare cell types. What is new is coupling morphology, text, transport, and isoform readouts with single-cell or spatial data, rather than treating any single modality as sufficient.
